caption.text:
We are so proud to stand beside these partners.

A few weeks ago in Washington, D.C., the Wild Beauty Foundation returned to Capitol Hill for another Lost Horses fly-in; meeting with Members of Congress and their staff to continue advancing protections for America’s horses.

We were joined by ASPCA, Animal Welfare Institute, 1/ST, The Jockey Club, and many others to raise awareness about the pipeline that claimed more than 25,000 horses in 2025 alone.

It was inspiring to be part of such collaboration and teamwork.

We were also honored to present Congresswoman Dina Titus with the Wild Beauty Foundation Legacy Award in recognition of her tireless work to protect America’s equines.

Thank you, Congresswoman Titus.

And thank you to every single person who has stood with The Lost Horses campaign.

Your letters, calls, shares, and engagement are truly making a difference. We know they are breaking through because just weeks ago, a legislative strategy we helped champion with our partners resulted in core SAFE Act protections advancing through the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee - a significant milestone to end horse slaughter.

The fight is far from over.  But we have extraordinary momentum, and together we are moving this issue forward.

In honor of our horses, even if you’ve already sent a letter, please send another today by clicking TAKE ACTION at losthorses.org.

No horse deserves to be lost again.

#TheLostHorses #WildBeautyFoundation #SAFEAct
